text: On the Humean picture that Bird opposes, a fundamental property has an intrinsic qualitative nature, a ___, that is independent of the causal or dispositional role the property happens to play.
explanation: A quiddity is the bare qualitative 'whatness' a Humean assigns to a property independently of its causal role, so that the laws connecting properties are contingent external additions. Bird rejects quidditism, holding instead that a property is constituted by its dispositional profile, which makes the associated laws metaphysically necessary.
